unknown_bugs.description: Channel name sanitization only replaces '/' and '..' but allows null bytes, control characters, and other dangerous filesystem characters. A channel name containing \x00 passes through the sanitizer unchanged, which can cause filesystem errors or security issues when used in file paths.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: BusWriter._channel_path('test\x00evil') returns a path containing a null byte. On some systems os.open() with a null byte in the path raises ValueError; on others it truncates at the null.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Use a whitelist approach: re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]', '_', channel) to only allow safe characters.

unknown_bugs.description: Proto B CommDir._check_canonical_match() compares self._requested != self._path using raw string equality, but self._requested may have a trailing slash that os.path.realpath() strips. Proto A uses os.path.realpath(self._requested) != self._path which is correct. This means Proto B falsely rejects valid paths that end with '/' or contain './'.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: CommDir(requested_path='/valid/path/').validate() raises CommDirError even though the path is valid. The trailing slash causes _requested != _path because realpath strips it.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Change the comparison to: if os.path.realpath(self._requested) != self._path, matching Proto A's approach.

unknown_bugs.description: Proto B CommDir._check_writable() uses os.access(path, os.W_OK) without handling root user. Proto A checks os.geteuid() == 0 and falls back to stat-based permission checks because os.access() always returns True for root. Proto B will incorrectly report non-writable directories as writable when run as root.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: As root, create a directory with 0o444 permissions. Proto B's _check_writable passes (os.access returns True for root). Proto A's _check_writable correctly fails (checks stat bits).
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Add the root user check from Proto A: if os.geteuid() == 0: check st_mode & 0o200.

unknown_bugs.description: Coordinator.stop() closes the SharedState connection but never unregisters itself from the agents table. The coordinator row remains with status='alive' and a stale heartbeat. Workers' CoordinatorWatchdog must wait for the heartbeat to expire (default 300s timeout) before detecting the coordinator is gone, even though stop() was called gracefully.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: Start coordinator, register workers with watchdog. Call coordinator.stop(). Workers wait up to 300 seconds before detecting coordinator death, even though the stop was intentional.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Add self._state.execute('UPDATE agents SET status="stopped" WHERE agent_id=?') before self._state.close() in stop(). Or add an unregister_agent method to SharedState.

unknown_bugs.description: Proto B CoordinatorWatchdog._monitor_loop() has no grace period for coordinator startup, unlike Proto A which implements a grace_deadline. If a worker starts before the coordinator, the Proto B watchdog will never fire death callbacks because coordinator_was_alive never becomes True (there's no transition from True to False). The worker hangs indefinitely waiting for a coordinator that crashed during startup.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: Start Proto B worker before coordinator. Coordinator crashes during startup before its first heartbeat. Watchdog never fires because coordinator_was_alive is always False. Worker waits forever.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Add a grace period matching Proto A: grace_deadline = time.time() + self._timeout. After grace_deadline expires with coordinator_was_alive still False, fire callbacks.

unknown_bugs.description: repair_bus_file() reads the file with open() (no file locking), filters corrupt lines, then writes a temp file and renames it. If a BusWriter appends a message between the read and the rename (using atomic O_APPEND), the appended message is lost because the rename overwrites the file with the snapshot taken before the append.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: Start repair_bus_file on a file with corrupt lines. While it's processing, a BusWriter.publish() appends a new valid message. The repair completes and renames, discarding the new message.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Acquire an exclusive flock on the bus file before reading and release after the rename. Or use a cooperative locking protocol between repair and write operations.

unknown_bugs.description: The simple YAML frontmatter parser cannot handle block-style (multi-line) list values. YAML lists using '- item' syntax on separate lines are parsed as separate key-value pairs with '-' prefix, resulting in incorrect metadata. Only inline [item1, item2] lists are supported.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: Create a KB entry with block-style tags: 'tags:\n  - python\n  - testing'. The parser sees 'tags:' with empty value (parsed as None) and '  - python' as an invalid key-value line.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Either document that only inline list syntax is supported, or enhance the parser to detect indented '- item' lines following a key with empty value and collect them into a list.

unknown_bugs.description: validate_scripts() calls scripts_dir.iterdir() at line 233 to check for orphan files, but does not verify the directory exists first. If storage/scripts/ is missing or was renamed, iterdir() raises FileNotFoundError, crashing the entire validation run.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: Run validate-storage.py when the scripts/ directory doesn't exist. FileNotFoundError crashes the script instead of reporting a validation error.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Wrap the orphan file check in 'if scripts_dir.is_dir():' guard, similar to how kb_validator.py checks entries_dir.is_dir().

unknown_bugs.description: detect_cycles_dfs() uses recursive DFS with no depth limit. For deep dependency chains (>1000 nodes), this hits Python's default recursion limit and raises RecursionError, crashing the checker instead of reporting an error.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: Create a knowledge base with >1000 KB entries in a linear builds_on chain (KB-0001 -> KB-0002 -> ... -> KB-1500). Running cross_ref_checker crashes with RecursionError.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Convert to an iterative DFS using an explicit stack, or add sys.setrecursionlimit() with a try/except RecursionError fallback.

unknown_bugs.description: SharedState.heartbeat() updates last_heartbeat for a given agent_id but does not check whether the UPDATE affected any rows. If the agent_id was never registered, the UPDATE silently affects 0 rows and returns None. The caller has no way to detect that the heartbeat had no effect, potentially masking registration failures.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: state.heartbeat('nonexistent-agent') returns None with no error. The agent's heartbeat loop thinks it's working fine but no heartbeat is actually recorded.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Check cursor.rowcount after UPDATE and return a boolean (True if updated, False if agent not found), or raise ValueError. Proto B's SharedStateMap.heartbeat() already returns a boolean.

unknown_bugs.description: SharedState.close() has no guard against double-close. If close() is called twice, the second call tries to close an already-closed sqlite3.Connection. Depending on the sqlite3 version, this may raise ProgrammingError. Other modules in the codebase (coordinator_hub.py, direct_channels.py) use a _closed flag to guard against this.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: state = SharedState(path); state.close(); state.close() -- may raise ProgrammingError on the second call.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Add a self._closed = False flag in __init__ and check it in close(): if self._closed: return; self._closed = True.

unknown_bugs.description: Proto B CommConfig is missing the busy_timeout_ms parameter that Proto A CommConfig has. This cross-prototype API inconsistency means code written against Proto A's CommConfig that accesses config.busy_timeout_ms will break when used with Proto B's CommConfig. It also means Proto B has no standard way to configure timeout-related behavior.
unknown_bugs.reproduction: config = CommConfig(comm_dir='/path'); config.busy_timeout_ms raises AttributeError. Proto A: config.busy_timeout_ms returns 30000.
unknown_bugs.fix_suggestion: Add busy_timeout_ms: int = 30_000 to Proto B's CommConfig, even if it's unused by mmap operations, for API compatibility.

cross_module_inconsistencies.issue: Proto A _check_no_tmp checks BOTH self._requested and self._path against /tmp. Proto B only checks self._path. A symlink from /tmp/x -> /safe/dir would pass Proto B's check but fail Proto A's.

Proto A _check_canonical_match uses os.path.realpath(self._requested) != self._path. Proto B uses self._requested != self._path (raw string comparison). Proto B is stricter and rejects valid paths with trailing slashes or redundant separators.
Proto A _check_writable handles root user (euid==0) with stat-based checks. Proto B uses only os.access() which is unreliable for root.
Proto A CoordinatorWatchdog has a grace period (grace_deadline) for coordinator startup. Proto B CoordinatorWatchdog does not, causing workers to hang forever if coordinator never starts.

Proto A check_agents() returns list[dict] (agent['agent_id']). Proto B check_agents() returns list[AgentSlotView] (agent.agent_id). Code copied between prototypes will crash due to dict-vs-attribute access mismatch.

Proto A SharedState.heartbeat() returns None regardless of success. Proto B SharedStateMap.heartbeat() returns bool. Callers must handle both conventions, and Proto A callers cannot detect unregistered agents.
Proto A CommConfig has busy_timeout_ms field. Proto B CommConfig does not. Cross-prototype code that accesses this field will break on Proto B.
